# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the manual, but I speak into a void this turn — Blind speaks first, then Blind, then Deaf, and I only reach Deaf via gesture (Blind can't see gestures, and I can't speak to convey words anyway). I have no information yet from Deaf about what light is on, so I have nothing useful to send. I should wait and gather info first: I need Deaf to tell me (via gesture, since I can see gestures) what light color they see, then I can gesture back the correct wire color to... wait, actually I can't gesture to Blind either usefully since Blind can't see. I need to relay through Deaf isn't right either — Deaf can't hear me, but I can gesture to Deaf, and Deaf can see my gestures. But Blind needs the info and Blind can't see gestures or hear me.

So the only path to Blind is: Deaf sees the bomb, Deaf could speak (Deaf can speak and both Blind and Mute could hear if unnamed) — Deaf can tell Blind the light color by speaking. Then I need to give the manual mapping to someone who can relay it to Blind by speech — that's Deaf, since Deaf can hear my... no, Deaf cannot hear. I cannot speak at all.

Actually only Deaf can speak-to-inform Blind (since Blind can only hear). I need to get the manual's mapping to Deaf via gesture, then Deaf can see the light and speak the correct wire color to Blind. I'll wait this turn since I have no info about which light yet, but I can preemptively gesture the full manual mapping to Deaf using a symbol code.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is red. Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green.

Deaf can't hear me, so speech is useless toward them — I must gesture. Deaf sees the bomb: light is red. Per manual, red light → cut red wire. Wire 1 is red. I need to signal "wire 1" or "red" to Deaf via gesture so Deaf can then speak the correct instruction to Blind (since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear).

I'll establish a simple gesture code: point up (☝) for "wire one", or better, use a distinct symbol to mean "cut this one" pointing at position. Since I can't reference their wire numbers directly with words, I'll use numeric gestures: ☝ = wire 1, ✌ = wire 2, 🤟 = wire 3 (three fingers). I'll gesture ☝ to indicate wire 1 is correct.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green, display shows 0, light is red
Deaf says to Mute: I saw your gesture, one finger. Display still 0, light red, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. Tell me what to do with gestures, one symbol at a time.

Deaf understood my gesture (☝ = one/first) and is asking me to confirm via gesture which wire to cut. Light is red → manual says cut red wire → wire 1 is red. My ☝ already correctly pointed to wire 1. I should confirm this clearly so Deaf can then speak "cut wire 1" to Blind.

I'll gesture ☝ again to confirm wire 1 is the one to cut, unambiguously.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Received one finger again, I am telling blind about wire 1. Confirm with two fingers if you want a different wire, or thumbs up if wire 1 is correct.

Deaf is asking for explicit confirmation: thumbs up if wire 1 is correct. Wire 1 is indeed correct (red light → red wire → wire 1 is red). I'll confirm with 👍.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
